REGULATION ON PROCEDURE
FOR ADMISSIONS AT JKLU
Our University has adopted standard procedure for admitting the students in various programmes.
The procedure for Admissions is based on the prescribed guidelines of the regulating authority as well as Supreme Court of India.
All possible care has been taken to abide by the necessary guidelines.
The whole process is divided into 3 stages for clarity and transparency.
Stage 1
Admissions Division shall undertake various activities for promotion of the programmes offered by the University. These activities would include:
• Visit to various degree colleges, schools and coaching centres.
• Participation in Fairs.
• Organize counseling meets to educate the students and their parents about our University and its offerings.
• Give detailed information to aspirants about each programme offered by the University.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
• Give detailed information to aspirants about each programme offered by the University.
• Conduct campaign on social networking sites.
• Ensure installation of hoardings / kiosks at decided spots.
• Pay attention to the prospective students and their parents when they are on campus. Take them around the campus. Arrange their meeting with faculty, Director-IM/Director-IET, Vice Chancellor or any other authorized person on the campus, if required.
• Organize other activities for promotion as advised by the competent authority from time to time.
• Submit media plan to the Vice Chancellor.
• Maintain record of the applications, brochures, handouts, pamphlets and any other promotional material used for the purpose of admission.
• Maintain record of the filled up applications received from the candidates.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
• Maintain record of the filled up applications received from the candidates.
• Send all the filled up applications to Director-IM or Director-IET based on the programme applied for by the candidate.
Stage 2
• Office of the Director-IM/Director-IET shall maintain the record of all the filled up applications received from various sources.
All steps in terms of Written Test, Group Discussion, Personal Interview / Counselling shall be undertaken by the Admissions Committee of each Institute headed by the respective Director as Chairperson.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
• Director of each Institute shall forward for approval of the Vice Chancellor the names of eligible and suitable candidates for admission in various programmes after undertaking all the steps prescribed by the Supreme Court of India and AICTE in terms of Written Test, Group Discussion, Personal Interview / Counselling.
Stage 3
• Record of the list of candidates recommended for admission by Director of each Institute shall be maintained by the office of the Vice Chancellor.
• After approval of the Vice Chancellor, the list of the candidates who are offered admission shall be displayed by Director of each Institute on the Notice Boards.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
• The students shall be advised to report for registration on a particular day decided by the University. The Roll List will be prepared based on the details of registered candidates.
• The registration shall be followed by Invocation, Induction and commencement of the classes.
• The list of registered candidates, who shall now onwards be addressed as students, shall be forwarded by Director of each Institute to the Accounts Section with a copy to the Registrar of the University within one week after registration.
• The Admission Process ends here.

REGULATION ON
STUDENT ATTENDANCE
1.
Every student is expected to put in 100% attendance.
The minimum attendance for appearing in End Term examination for every student is 75% in every course.
A student, who has attendance lower than 75%, will not be permitted to appear in the End Term Semester examination of the course(s) in which the shortfall exists.
2.
Every faculty member teaching a course shall take attendance till the last day of instruction in the Semester in the attendance sheet provided for the same and finalize the attendance secured by the student.
In addition, the attendance will also be marked through ERP.
3.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
In addition, the attendance will also be marked through ERP.
3.
Since regular attendance and punctuality in the classes is compulsory, leave can be granted to a student by the Director of the Institute on genuine reasons, not exceeding 25% of the total classes held during the Semester under any circumstances.
4.
Absence without leave will not be permitted beyond 10% of the classes during a Semester.
Once the student exceeds 8% of absence without leave during the Semester, the student will be warned by the Institute under intimation to the Academic Section for informing the parent of the student.
5.
The details of all students who have attendance less than 75% in a particular course will be announced in the class by the faculty himself/ herself every month.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:

7.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:

Condonation of Attendance: Those students who have availed medical leave on valid grounds or any other valid reason may be considered for condonation of attendance provided the percentage of attendance excluding the period of medical leave is not below 75% and their overall attendance including the period of illness/absence for other valid reason does not fall below 65%.
All cases shall be reviewed by the Director of the respective Institute and the recommendations discussed with the Vice Chancellor for condonation.
8. The condonation of attendance has to be got approved at least ten days prior to the commencement of the End Term Examination.
9.

Those students will not be allowed to appear in the End Term Examinations.
10.

text:

12.

If a student who has not been allowed to appear in the End Term Examination due to deficiency in attendance in a course, he/she shall be awarded “I” grade (where “I” stands for incomplete for want of minimum attendance) in that course.
This grade shall appear in the Grade Card till the course is successfully completed.
13.
A student awarded “I” grade in a course has to clear it compulsorily when the course is offered next.
However, he will be allowed a maximum of two attempts including the first attempt to clear the course.
If the student fails to clear the course in two attempts, he may not be allowed to continue in the programme.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:

However, if the student secures two or more “I” grades in the second Semester or thereafter, he may not be allowed to continue in the programme.

GENERAL GUIDELINES FOR THE AWARD OF GRADES The following are the general guidelines for the award of grades: (a) All evaluations of different components of a course shall be done in marks assigned for the course for each student.
(b) The marks of various components viz., Mid-Term Examination I and II, End-Term Examination, Internal Assignments, Quiz for the Theory Papers, Practicals and Sessionals, shall be as per the Scheme of Teaching and Examination approved by the Academic Council and scaled to a 100-points scale.

(d) The University shall be following Relative Grading Scheme for all courses of the Programmes offered by various Institutes, where the number of students is more than 10.

The Grading Scheme to be followed in all Programmes of the University is given as under: (i) “Highest Marks obtained by a student in the class in a particular course will be treated equivalent to 100 per cent marks.
Students having obtained 85 per cent and above marks of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘A’ Grade.
Students having obtained 70 per cent and above but below 85 per cent of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘B’ Grade.
Students having obtained 55 per cent and above but below 70 per cent of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘C’ Grade.
Students having obtained 40 per cent and above but below 55 per cent of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘D’ Grade.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
Students having obtained 40 per cent and above but below 55 per cent of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘D’ Grade.
Students having obtained below 40 per cent marks of the highest scorer will be awarded ‘F’ Grade”.
(ii) Pass Grade is D and above (Grade F is a fail grade).
(iii) The student has to clear both theory and lab components independently to consider 60:40 ratio of obtained marks for awarding pass grade for that course.
If the student fails either in theory or in lab component, he/she shall be awarded ‘F’ in that course.
(iv) Illustration (a) If a student has obtained 80 marks in a course which is highest in the class, then for that course 80 marks will be treated equivalent to 100 per cent.

Learning Resource Centre
Rules & Regulations
1. About LRC
The Learning Resource Centre (LRC) came into existence as a constituent of the JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur.
The aim of the LRC is to serve the needs of the Faculty, Research Scholars, Students and External Members of the LRC.
It is heart of the University and acts as a centre for the collection of literature predominantly related to management, engineering and technology and its allied subjects and develops a comprehensive collection of information that is useful for teaching and reference purposes.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
User satisfaction is the prime objective of LRC services.
Library is situated in a multi-story building with growing collection of Books, Journals and other reading materials.
LRC is subscribing wide range of national and international periodicals and journals, in addition to an impressive collection of databases such as EBSCO, corporate & technical annual reports and CDs, ETintelligence Service, CII (Confederation of Indian Industry) publications, IEEE Transactions and ASME (American Society of Mechanical Engineers) Publications.
LRC is also in the process of subscribing databases such as Science Direct, ACSE (American Society of Civil Engineers) Publications etc.
Learning Resource Centre (LRC) is managed by KOHA software integrated with ERP system of the University.
It is web based integrated library system installed on Linux platform.
title: JKLU Regulations (examination, grading, attendance)

text:
It is web based integrated library system installed on Linux platform.
KOHA is equipped with Acquisition, Cataloging, Circulation, Serial Control and OPAC modules.
It supports MARC21 and UNIMARC for professional cataloguing and z39.50 for copy cataloguing from reputed libraries.
OPAC module provides access to the library catalogue.
Through this module, users of the library will also be able to check their borrowing details, reserved items, make suggestions for new books, and update their personal details as well as add tags to books of their liking.
This module provides a simple and clear
search interface. Users are able to search through all fields of the database as well as within specific fields.

2. Resources
LRC has a collection of books, journals and other reading materials in the area of Management, Engineering, Humanities and Social Sciences and allied subjects taught in the University.

REGULATION ON STUDENT ATTENDANCE
1.
Every student is expected to put in 100% attendance.
The minimum attendance for appearing in Mid Term Examination/s and End Term Examination for every student is 75% in every course.
A student, who has attendance lower than 75%, will not be permitted to appear in the Mid Term Examination/s and End Term Examination of the course(s) in which the shortfall exists.
2.
Every faculty member teaching a course shall take attendance during the Semester till the last day of instruction before Mid Term Examination/s and End Term Examination in the attendance sheet provided for the same and finalize the attendance secured by the student.
In addition, the attendance will also be marked through ERP.
3.

3.
Since regular attendance and punctuality in the classes in compulsory, leave can be granted to a student by the Director of the Institute on genuine reasons, not exceeding 25% of the total classes held during the Semester under any circumstances.
4.
Absence without leave will not be permitted beyond 10% of the classes during a Semester.
Once the student exceeds 8% of absence without leave during the Semester, the student will be warned by the Institute under intimation to the Academic section for informing the parent of the student.
5.
The details of all students who have attendance less than 75% in a particular course will be announced in the class by the faculty himself/ herself every month.

(i) The marks of the backlog student shall not be considered for calculating the relative marks in respect of the highest marks of the complete batch/all the students appearing in the respective course.

(j) However, if the course has been discontinued in the next batch, a separate question paper shall be set by the respective faculty for the backlog students.

About JKLU
Our academic journey is based on intellectual stimulation and experiential learning.
Founded in 2011, JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU) continues JK Group's 140-year legacy of excellence and commitment to nation-building.
Accredited with an 'A' grade by NAAC, JKLU is at the forefront of innovation, blending academia with industry through its interdisciplinary programs in engineering, management, and design that prepare students to excel in an ever-evolving workspace.
JKLU's faculty includes accomplished scholars from globally renowned institutions such as the IIMs, IITs, NIDs, and other top universities worldwide.
The university’s curriculum focuses on interdisciplinary learning, hands-on projects, and practical problem-solving, providing students with the flexibility and choice of tools they need to address complex challenges and drive a meaningful change.
title: About

text:
The university's strong industry connections, real-world projects, and immersive internships form a core part of the JKLU experience, bridging the gap between academic knowledge and practical application.
Through strategic partnerships and exchange opportunities with leading institutions in India and abroad, students gain a global perspective that enriches their education and broadens their horizons.
At JKLU, students also benefit from access to cutting-edge centers such as the Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking, the Atal Incubation Centre, and the AIMA BizLab.
These platforms foster innovation, entrepreneurship, and critical inquiry, encouraging students to explore new ideas and develop a problem-solving mindset.
With state-of-the-art facilities, a vibrant campus community, and a culture that nurtures talent, JKLU empowers students to become leaders, innovators, and changemakers, poised to make a positive impact on society.

Internal Quality Assurance Cell
As mandated by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), JK Lakshmipat University has established the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as a pivotal measure for sustaining quality.
The primary role of the IQAC is to oversee the initiation, planning, implementation, and monitoring of various quality enhancement activities across the university.
IQAC’S core mission is to infuse quality into every aspect of the educational process—from input and process to output—ensuring comprehensive quality enhancement.
Objectives
Promote the integration of universal quality principles in the university's operational functions.
Develop and implement policies, programs, and systems that align with both national and international quality standards.
Continuously monitor and evaluate the efficacy of quality improvement initiatives, including accreditation processes, certification, and rankings.

Clearly define roles, responsibilities, and authority across the university, setting measurable objectives for various functions and levels.
Establish robust systems for the collection and analysis of data to monitor various university processes.
Develop strategies for ongoing improvement by understanding the university's context, including stakeholder needs and expectations, and identifying potential risks and opportunities.

text:
Milestones
Our academic journey is based on intellectual stimulation and experiential learning.
Established in 2011 by the JK Group, JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU) was envisioned as a pioneering institution that bridges the gap between industry and academia while equipping young minds to thrive in a rapidly evolving world.
With a distinguished legacy spanning over 140 years, the JK Group has played a significant role in India's industrial and social development.
Today, it stands among the country’s most respected industrial and philanthropic conglomerates, with contributions across sectors such as textiles, tyres, cement, paper, education, and community development.
Its enduring success is rooted in a steadfast commitment to excellence, integrity, and empowerment.
JKLU reflects this spirit of purposeful progress.

Vision & Mission
Our Vision
To be one of India’s most innovative higher education institutions.
Innovation in education means more than just incorporating new technologies; it is about creating an environment where curiosity thrives, creativity flourishes, and boundaries are pushed.
We aim to lead by example in fostering a learning culture that transcends traditional classroom methods, embracing interdisciplinary learning, hands-on experiences, and real-world problem-solving.
At the heart of our vision is the belief that every student has the potential to create a meaningful impact on the world.
In pursuing this vision, we aspire to be recognised not only for academic excellence but also for our contribution to shaping the future of education in India and beyond.
Mission
title: Vision & Mission

Mission
To realise its vision, the University will: Practice teaching that inculcates critical thinking and problem solving.
Our pedagogy will be designed to enable every student to develop advanced levels of critical thinking and problem-solving abilities as these skills are essential for driving innovations that can usher in meaningful transformations.
Pursue research that leads to innovation and enhancement of real-life applications.
The university is committed to empowering its faculty and students to pursue research that advances knowledge in domains that are critical to betterment of the society and sustainability of the world.
Offer experience that leads to all-round development.

text:
Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking
The Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking (CCCT) is a key innovation of JK Lakshmipat University which is integral to innovative pedagogies practised on campus.
The CCCT integrates liberal arts, scientific temperament, group dynamics, and interpersonal communication to support students’ personal and professional growth.
Through a combination of credited courses, communication labs, and diverse events, the CCCT enhances students' capacity in critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication, preparing them for both career and life.
Courses
The CCCT supplements students’ learning journeys through six unique credited courses focused on capacity building in communication, critical thinking, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making.
These courses are embedded as core components across the three institutes of the university, ensuring that students, regardless of their discipline, gain essential cognitive and communication skills.
title: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking
section: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking

text:
An Active Learning Approach is employed in these courses, engaging students in activities that allow them to practice and refine their skills instead of merely absorbing theoretical knowledge.
Fundamentals of Communication
This course provides an introduction to the importance of effective communication, the consequences of poor communication, and the different elements of verbal and non-verbal communication. Students learn about, and enhance, the components of communication: kinesics, paralanguage (voice) and language.
Critical Thinking and Storytelling
The modern world offers confounding opinions and choices that need to be navigated judiciously. This course explores frameworks and processes to critically examine narratives, reconstruct them, and craft well-reasoned stories that can be told using impactful communication.
Perspectives on Contemporary Issues
title: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking

text:
Perspectives on Contemporary Issues
In an era of globalization, there is an increasing need for the youth to be able to empathize with others, value diverse perspectives and cultures and understand how events around the world are intertwined.
Global issues revolve around social, economic and environmental factors which ultimately add to the interconnectedness of countries.
In this course, students will employ key critical thinking concepts to analyze contemporary issues from multiple perspectives.
They will explore the impact at micro and macro levels.
Understanding and Managing Conflict
In today’s increasingly complex and fragmented world, it is important to be able to resolve conflicts and build healthy relationships.
title: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking

text:
Understanding and Managing Conflict
In today’s increasingly complex and fragmented world, it is important to be able to resolve conflicts and build healthy relationships.
Interpersonal and Group Dynamics is a course designed to prepare students to identify conflicts, manage emotions, analyze the situation and characters, and practice different frameworks to deal with conflicts.
Communication and Identity
This course enables students to explore their personal and professional identities, to create their distinctive presence.
It intends to help them gain an understanding of the basic purpose, benefits, and responsibilities of self-presence, and to begin the process of defining their values, strengths, and goals.
Critical Thinking for Decisions at Workplace
In today's world, the idea of right and wrong is being challenged by businesses, use of technology, economic conditions, and norms of societies.
title: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking

text:
In today's world, the idea of right and wrong is being challenged by businesses, use of technology, economic conditions, and norms of societies.
The relevance of a well-reasoned decision is crucial.

Borrowing LRC Materials

KOHA - Library Management System
LRC resources are managed through KOHA, a web-based integrated library system installed on a Linux platform.
KOHA streamlines library operations, providing modules for acquisition, cataloging, circulation, serial control, and OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue).
This system supports MARC21 and UNIMARC standards for professional cataloging and z39.50 for copy cataloging from renowned libraries.
KOHA’s user-friendly interface simplifies the search process, enabling users to search across all fields or within specific categories to find the resources they need.

text:
Life in Jaipur
A Historic City, A Modern Student Experience
For students at JK Lakshmipat University, life in Jaipur offers the best of both worlds—a city steeped in history, yet brimming with youth, culture, and creativity.
From ancient forts and bustling bazaars to contemporary cafes and art spaces, Jaipur is a canvas of contrasts—rich in tradition but always evolving.
A Hub of Art, Design, and Innovation
Jaipur is not just about palaces and monuments.
It’s a UNESCO Creative City, known for its thriving craft and design industries.
Students, especially those pursuing design, technology, management, and entrepreneurship, find the city to be a living lab—full of opportunities to engage with startups, exhibitions, studios, and cultural events that reflect India’s creative and economic dynamism.
Culinary Adventures at Every Corner
title: Student Life In Jaipur - Culture, Food & Getaways

text:
Culinary Adventures at Every Corner
From traditional Rajasthani thalis to global fusion cuisine, Jaipur offers a delightful culinary journey.
Local favourites like dal baati churma, kachoris, and lassi sit comfortably next to Korean cafes, Italian bistros, and vegan smoothie bars.
For JKLU students, food outings are more than just meals—they’re social rituals, cultural explorations, and mood-lifters after long studio or coding hours.
Getaways & Exploration Beyond Campus
Weekends in Jaipur are never dull.
You can hike up to Nahargarh Fort for a panoramic sunset view, cycle along the Aravalli trails, or shop for handmade textiles and jewellery at Bapu Bazaar.
For those who crave the outdoors, destinations like Pushkar, Ranthambore, and Udaipur are just a few hours away - perfect for short student trips or solo adventures.
title: Student Life In Jaipur - Culture, Food & Getaways

text:
Modern Living with Easy Access
With excellent road, rail, and air connectivity, Jaipur makes travel easy for students visiting home or planning internships and conferences in other cities.
Ride-sharing apps, local buses, and metro services provide affordable and reliable transport, while modern malls, bookstores, theatres, and co-working cafes ensure students have everything they need to balance work and play.
Discover Jaipur. Discover Yourself
Life at JKLU is inseparable from the life Jaipur offers.
It’s a place to grow independently, build friendships, and immerse yourself in a city that respects the past but dreams big for the future.
Whether you're here to build your career, find your voice, or chase an idea - Jaipur gives you the space and spark to do it all.

Student Councils
When you choose JKLU, you become part of a diverse community.
The Student Councils at JK Lakshmipat University is made up of elected representatives from the Institutes of Engineering and Technology, Management, and Design.
The councils are dedicated to enhancing campus life and bridging the gap between students and administration. They advocate for students’ interests, provide a platform for expression, and oversee university activities, events, clubs, and student services.
-->
Academic Affairs
The Councils of Academic Affairs serves as the bridge between students and the administration, ensuring clear communication and addressing academic concerns.
It gathers feedback to improve the academic experience, resolves issues, and advocates for better academic services, creating a supportive environment where students can thrive.
Campus Life
title: Student Councils At JKLU

text:
Campus Life
The Councils of Campus Life focuses on enhancing the overall student experience at JKLU.
It oversees housing, dining, and transportation, ensuring smooth day-to-day operations.
The Councils encourages open dialogue among students and works with the administration to create an inclusive and engaging campus environment.
Cultural Affairs
The Councils of Cultural Affairs enriches campus life by organizing cultural events and promoting student involvement in community service. It fosters creativity, diversity, and collaboration, ensuring a dynamic cultural atmosphere and creating opportunities for students to showcase their talents.
Technical Affairs
The Councils of Technical Affairs oversees the university’s technology infrastructure, ensuring its reliability and security. It works to improve the campus’s technological solutions, enhances academic experiences through tech, and promotes sustainability with eco-friendly innovations.
Sports
title: Student Councils At JKLU

text:
Sports
The Councils of Sports manages sports facilities, organizes events, and encourages student participation in both recreational and competitive sports.
It fosters a healthy, active lifestyle and supports student-athletes, ensuring they receive the recognition they deserve while promoting team spirit across campus.
Public Relations
The Councils of Public Relations promotes JKLU’s brand and builds connections with industry professionals, alumni, and placement agencies to create job opportunities for students.
It manages the university’s social media and communications, enhancing its visibility and strengthening relationships with external stakeholders.
Members
This year, the Student Councils is defined by its diverse and inclusive representation.
With 56 members, the councils features nearly equal participation from both girls and boys (32 girls and 24 boys), demonstrating a commitment to equality and inclusivity.
title: Student Councils At JKLU

text: The councils also has strong representation across all three institutions and academic years, with 19 third-year students, 16 second-year students, and 15 first-year students.

Atal Incubation Centre – JK Lakshmipat University ( AIC-JKLU ) was established in 2019 with the support of Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, and JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU).
Over the last six years, AIC-JKLU has supported 200+ startups across diverse sectors including Energy Innovation, Eldercare & Longevity, and Sustainability-focused Materials and Solutions. It has consistently ranked among the top-performing incubation centers under the AIM network.
What sets AIC-JKLU apart is its interdisciplinary access — with more than 33 state-of-the-art labs in design, engineering, and computing, a pool of 45+ expert mentors, and corporate partners that support both startup pilots and industry collaborations.

Pedagogy
The Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking (CCCT) is a key innovation of JK Lakshmipat University which is integral to innovative pedagogies practised on campus.
The CCCT integrates liberal arts, scientific temperament, group dynamics, and interpersonal communication to support students’ personal and professional growth.
Through a combination of credited courses, communication labs, and diverse events, the CCCT enhances students' capacity in critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication, preparing them for both career and life.
Courses
The CCCT supplements students’ learning journeys through six unique credited courses focused on capacity building in communication, critical thinking, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making.
title: Centre For Communication & Critical Thinking
section: Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking

text:
Courses
The CCCT supplements students’ learning journeys through six unique credited courses focused on capacity building in communication, critical thinking, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making.
These courses are embedded as core components across the three institutes of the university, ensuring that students, regardless of their discipline, gain essential cognitive and communication skills.
An Active Learning Approach is employed in these courses, engaging students in activities that allow them to practice and refine their skills instead of merely absorbing theoretical knowledge.
Fundamentals of Communication
This course provides an introduction to the importance of effective communication, the consequences of poor communication, and the different elements of verbal and non-verbal communication. Students learn about, and enhance, the components of communication: kinesics, paralanguage (voice) and language.
Critical Thinking and Storytelling
title: Centre For Communication & Critical Thinking

text:
Critical Thinking and Storytelling
The modern world offers confounding opinions and choices that need to be navigated judiciously. This course explores frameworks and processes to critically examine narratives, reconstruct them, and craft well-reasoned stories that can be told using impactful communication.
Perspectives on Contemporary Issues
In an era of globalization, there is an increasing need for the youth to be able to empathize with others, value diverse perspectives and cultures and understand how events around the world are intertwined.
Global issues revolve around social, economic and environmental factors which ultimately add to the interconnectedness of countries.
In this course, students will employ key critical thinking concepts to analyze contemporary issues from multiple perspectives.
They will explore the impact at micro and macro levels.
Understanding and Managing Conflict
title: Centre For Communication & Critical Thinking

text:
They will explore the impact at micro and macro levels.
Understanding and Managing Conflict
In today’s increasingly complex and fragmented world, it is important to be able to resolve conflicts and build healthy relationships.
Interpersonal and Group Dynamics is a course designed to prepare students to identify conflicts, manage emotions, analyze the situation and characters, and practice different frameworks to deal with conflicts.
Communication and Identity
This course enables students to explore their personal and professional identities, to create their distinctive presence.
It intends to help them gain an understanding of the basic purpose, benefits, and responsibilities of self-presence, and to begin the process of defining their values, strengths, and goals.
Critical Thinking for Decisions at Workplace
title: Centre For Communication & Critical Thinking

text:
Critical Thinking for Decisions at Workplace
In today's world, the idea of right and wrong is being challenged by businesses, use of technology, economic conditions, and norms of societies.
The relevance of a well-reasoned decision is crucial.
This course intends to make students take better decisions keeping in mind purpose, context, and ethics.
Labs
Together with courses, the CCCT offers a 10-12-hour compulsory Communication Laboratory where students receive personalised guidance in thinking, writing, and speaking.
The lab is structured into four interactive formats:
Reading Circles
Think
Encouraging analytical reading and discussion.
Focused Groups
Write
Enhancing structured and effective writing skills.
Public Speaking
Speak
Developing confidence in verbal communication.

Biography
Afreen is an Assistant Professor at the Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking, JK Lakshmipat University.
Afreen is a recipient of the ICSSR Doctoral Fellowship and MCRG- Rosa Luxemburg Grant for research on pastoralism.
He has been awarded a Gold Medal for his Master’s in Public Administration and has qualified UGC-NET in Political Science.
Afreen is a founding member and lead organiser of the Peoples of Himalayas Academic Discourse Network and a member of the Ecologies of Labour network.
His interests lie in utilising Political-Economy to analyse shifts in Labour Practices and Mobility amongst nomadic communities in the Western Himalayas.

text:
His interests lie in utilising Political-Economy to analyse shifts in Labour Practices and Mobility amongst nomadic communities in the Western Himalayas.
He aims to decolonise epistemes and pedagogies and empower academic scholars belonging to the Western Himalayas.
His work on Covid, nomads and mobility has been published in edited volumes by Routledge and Lexington.
Afreen believes that a well cooked meal can be a potent challenge to bigotry, and a heartfelt poem can be a good tool for introspection.

Biography
Dr.
Akshat Agrawal holds a B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering from Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) and an M.Tech from USICT, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University (GGSIPU), New Delhi.
He earned his PhD from USICT, GGSIPU, New Delhi.
Prior to joining JKLU’s Institute of Engineering and Technology, he worked as a Cluster Lead at the School of Computer Science & Engineering, IILM University, Gurugram and, served as an Assistant Professor at Amity University Haryana.
Dr.
Agrawal has over 17 years of teaching and research experience.
His primary research interests include Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning, Artificial Neural Networks, Speech Processing, and Image Processing.
He has published 67 research papers in Scopus/SCIE-indexed international journals and conferences.

Biography
Amitanshu Shrivastava is an Assistant Professor at the JKLU Institute of Design, with over a decade of expertise in product design, creative storytelling, and education.
He is passionate about merging traditional Indian crafts with modern design principles to create innovative and engaging solutions.
A significant focus of his work is the design and development of educational games and puzzles, which inspire curiosity, foster learning, and encourage creative problem-solving among both children and adults.
As the founder of Ubiquitous Objects , Amitanshu has led diverse projects that celebrate cultural heritage, innovation, and play.
His work often involves creating meaningful experiences that bridge the gap between design and education, making learning an engaging and enjoyable journey.

Biography

Anshu Yadav is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Engineering & Technology.
She obtained her Ph.D. in Mathematics from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi in 2024, where her research focused on entropy stable numerical schemes for conservation laws and non-conservative hyperbolic systems.
Her research interests lie in Computational Mathematics, Numerical Analysis, Hyperbolic Partial Differential Equations, Entropy Stable Schemes, Finite Difference Methods, and Scientific Computing.
Her work has been published in reputed international journals including the Journal of Scientific Computing, Computers & Mathematics with Applications, and the Journal of Computational Physics.

Dr. Anusha Hegde
Assistant Professor
Biography
Dr.
Anusha Hegde is an Assistant Professor at the Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking, Institute of Management, JKLU, with a specialization in English literature, feminist theory, and speculative fiction.
She holds a PhD from the Central University of Punjab, Bathinda (2025), where her doctoral research focused on female subjectivity, dystopian science fiction, and posthumanism.
She earned her MA in English from the Central University of Karnataka — where she was awarded the Gold Medal for academic excellence — and her BA in Journalism, English, and Psychology from NMKRV College, Bengaluru.
Her research spans feminism, posthumanism, science fiction, ecocriticism, philosophy, mythology, and children's and young adult literature.
Dr.

She has presented her work at numerous national and international conferences across India.
Beyond her scholarly output, Dr.
Hegde has been invited as a keynote speaker and resource person at academic seminars and lecture series, and has served as an editorial member for The Ornate Circle and a reviewer for the International Humanities Research Nexus.
She also publishes creative writing, with short stories featured in The Children's Magazine since 2014.

Dr.
Ashish Jain is an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur since August 2025.
He has about 19 years of teaching experience.

(CSE) with distinction from Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya, Indore, India in 2008.
He earned his Ph.D.
(CSE) from Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Indore, India in 2018.
In his academic career, he has taught Data Structures and Algorithms, Cryptography, Design and Analysis of Algorithms, C Programming Language, and Soft Computing at engineering institutions in India.

Biography
Mr.
Ashutosh Kumar is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur.
He has about ten years of teaching and four years of research experience.
He completed his B.E. in Computer Science and Engineering from Rajiv Gandhi Prodyogiki Vishwavidyalaya, Bhopal in 2010, and an M.Tech in Information Technology (Networking) from VIT University, Vellore, in 2012.
He is pursuing his Ph.D.
(Thesis Submitted) from the Indian Institute of Information Technology Allahabad (IIITA) where his research focuses on IoT device security auditing and secure communication techniques.
His broader research interests span Cybersecurity, IoT Security, Network Security, and Penetration Testing, with particular emphasis on vulnerability assessment and security auditing of connected devices.

Biography
Dr.
Ashwini Sharma is currently Associate Professor at Institute of Management.
He has been associated with JKLU since 2010 and has since contributed significantly towards institution building in various roles and capacities.
He is an accomplished faculty in the area of IT/ IS, Data Analytics and General Management with over 23 years of teaching, research, training and administrative experience.
He has conducted numerous training programs for Executives of various organisations and is regularly invited as a Guest Faculty for FDPs conducted by a number of higher education institutes.
As a freelancer, he has successfully developed and implemented a number of information systems for organisations across various verticals like Automobiles, Pharmaceuticals, Paper, and Hospitality.
title: Dr. Ashwini Sharma, Associate Professor,

text:
As a freelancer, he has successfully developed and implemented a number of information systems for organisations across various verticals like Automobiles, Pharmaceuticals, Paper, and Hospitality.
He has also been associated with Container Corporation of India Limited for maintenance and enhancement of their information system.
Dr. Ashwini Sharma is on the Board of Studies of a number of Institutes and has also been empanelled as a Paper Setter and PhD Supervisor/ Examiner by a number of Universities.
He has varied teaching interests that include courses like Information Systems, Business Data Analysis, Research Methods, Statistics and Computer Programming.
He is a member of various professional bodies, such as Indian Society for Training and Development (ISTD), New Delhi; NHRD Network; Computer Society of India; Indian Science Congress Association and Insurance Institute of India.
title: Dr. Ashwini Sharma, Associate Professor,

text:
He has authored/ co-authored more than fifty publications that include research articles published in refereed national and international journals, case studies, monographs, books, research reports, and manuals.
Several case studies authored by him have been published by European Case Clearing House and have also been adopted by various publishers in their Case books.
He has attended over 100 conferences, seminars, and workshops and presented his research work at leading institutions across the country and abroad, such as Abu Dhabi University, UAE; IIM-Bangalore; IIM-Indore; IIM-Shillong, IIM-Ranchi, IIM-Amrtisar, IIM-Nagpur, AIMA, New Delhi; Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad to name a few.
He has also won Best Research Paper awards for three of his research publications at various international and national conferences.

Prof.
Jyoti Prakash Naidu is Dean (R&D) at JK Lakshmipat University.

Biography
Krishna Chaitanya Solasa received his PhD from the École Centrale School of Engineering at Mahindra University, Hyderabad, India, where he investigated the tribological behaviour of wear-resistant metal nitride coatings.
His earlier research during his master’s studies at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and the University at Buffalo focused on energy materials, smart and functional materials, and biomaterials.
His research interests include tribology, spectroscopy, materials science and materials characterization, with an emphasis on establishing structure-property-performance relationships of materials for mechanical, manufacturing, functional, and energy-related applications.

Mayank Kumar Kundalwal is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU), Jaipur.
He is currently pursuing his Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Jodhpur, where his research focuses on Machine Learning and Federated Learning, with particular emphasis on statistical heterogeneity, robustness, and privacy-preserving techniques in distributed learning systems.
He holds an M.Tech. from NIT Patna and a B.Tech. from Poornima University, Jaipur.
His broader research interests span deep learning, federated learning, and privacy-preserving AI, with applications in healthcare and other domains.

About
Dr.
Megha Sahu earned her Bachelor of Engineering degree in Electronics and Telecommunication from Bhilai Institute of Technology, Durg, Chhattisgarh (CSVTU Bhilai), India, in 2012.
She received her M.Tech. degree in Communication Systems from Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), Nagpur, Maharashtra, India, in 2015.
She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bhilai in 2022.She served as a visiting researcher at the ABB Research and Innovation Centre, Bangalore, India, and undertook a two-month internship as part of her PhD program.
With funding from SERB, Government of India, for her PhD work, she continued as a research associate at IIT Bhilai.
title: Dr. Megha Sahu , Assistant Professor,

text:
With funding from SERB, Government of India, for her PhD work, she continued as a research associate at IIT Bhilai.
During this period, she collaborated with industries on product-level implementation and participated in standardization activities with TSDSI, India, as a member of the SGSS Group.
Dr.
Sahu is a member of IEEE and IEEE ComSoc and actively serves as a reviewer for the prestigious IEEE Future Networks conference.
Her research interests span wireless communication and computer networks, with expertise in multi-access systems and protocols, traffic engineering, network coding, mobility management, optimization and reinforcement learning techniques, stochastic processes, queuing theory, systems architecture, telehealth, use case analysis, real-world network implementation, test cases, and product-level implementation.

nitya.pawar@jklu.edu.in
Dr. Nitya Pawar
Assistant Professor
Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking
Biography
Nitya Pawar holds a PhD in English from Ashoka University in India.
Her scholarly pursuits revolve around the profound world of Marathi bhakti focusing on the medieval Marathi saint-poet, Janabai and foregrounds bhakti saints as critical thinkers and translators.
Trained initially as an engineer at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar, she transitioned to the humanities through an M.A. in Society and Culture from the same place.
During this period, she produced a master's thesis on Sant Namdev, which laid the foundation for her current work on devotion, language, and translation.
She is especially interested in how acts of devotion and interpretation become sites of both personal and collective transformation through critical engagement.
title: Dr. Nitya Pawar, Assistant Professor, Centre For Communication And Critical Thinking

text:
She is especially interested in how acts of devotion and interpretation become sites of both personal and collective transformation through critical engagement.
Her scholarship, situated at the intersection of literary studies, translation theory, and cultural studies, has been presented at national and international platforms, with a co-authored forthcoming book-chapter in a Routledge volume on comparative mysticism.
She is also the recipient of the Society for Medieval Feminist Scholarship's Rising Star Grant for the year 2022–23.
Her work explores themes of mobility, caste, gender, and spirituality through the lens of translation, with broader interests in Indian Knowledge Systems, Indian Literature in Translation, pedagogical practices, and academic writing.

Biography
Dr Pranab Roy holds a PhD from Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur in the area of Computational Microfluidics with focus on EDA algorithms and Cyberphysical architecture.
In his academic career spanning more than 18 years, he has taught Object Oriented Programming, Computer Organization and Architecture, Embedded systems, Algorithm Design, Embedded systems, VLSI Physical Design, SoC Design and Data Structures with C and Java ,Mobile Application Development at Engineering institutions and Universities in India.
His research expertise is anchored around Algorithm design for EDA, Computational Microfluidics and Cognitive Computing.
His research contributions have been presented in leading international conferences and published in peer reviewed journals(IEEE, ACM, Springer and Elsevier).

Biography
Dr.
Rohit Singh is an Assistant Professor in the Institute of Engineering and Technology at JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU), Jaipur.
He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, where his doctoral research focused on secure authentication and communication in IoT environments.
He earned his M.Tech. in Computer Science and Engineering from NIT Hamirpur and B.Tech. in Information Technology from IIET Bareilly.
Before joining JKLU, he served as an Assistant Professor (Senior Scale) at Manipal University Jaipur.
title: Dr. Rohit Singh, Assistant Professor, Computer Science And Engineering

text:

His research contributions span peer-reviewed journals, conferences, book chapters, and patents, with applications in healthcare security, smart systems, and blockchain-based threat detection.
Alongside research, he is actively involved in student mentoring, internship coordination, and entrepreneurial initiatives, contributing to student learning, innovation, and professional development.

Biography
Dr. Sheetal Mundra is an economist and enthusiastic entrepreneurship educator with the aim to equip the new generations with economic life skills and providing them a platform to explore and develop their entrepreneurial skill.
She is a post-graduate and doctorate in economics (MDS University, Rajasthan) having 18 years of post-doctorate experience in teaching, training, and research.
Prior to JKLU, she served Northcap University, Gurgaon.
Being a merit holder, she is ‘Advance Data Analytics’ from IIM Kozhikode; FDP from IIM, Ahmedabad, certified in 'Digital Marketing and Analytics' from ISB; and 'Certified in Entrepreneurship Education’ by Wadhwani Foundation.
She has won Best Research Paper awards.
title: Dr. Sheetal Mundra, Acting Head, Economics And Entrepreneur

text:
She has won Best Research Paper awards.
Published more than two dozen research articles in International and National Journals and presented papers in international and national conferences organized by leading reputed Institutes (IIMA, IIML, MDI, IITR, FORE, NTU Singapore, Abu Dhabi University UAE, Symbiosis, etc.).
Authored one textbook and edited one book.
She has participated and organized various FDP's, MDP’s, Seminars, Workshops, Entrepreneurship Colloquium, and Entrepreneurship Seminars on various themes.
She is associated with start-up initiatives and actively collaborates and network with various institutions to build the entrepreneurship ecosystem at university.
She has mentored 80+ students’ start-ups.
She was a member of the Research Team of ‘The UK-India SME Knowledge Initiative’, sponsored by the British Council under the UKIERI.

Dr. Shubham Ranjan
Assistant Professor
Biography
Shubham Ranjan is an Assistant Professor at the Institute of Management, JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU), Jaipur.
He completed his Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi, with a doctoral thesis titled “Intersection of Gender and Diabetes in India: Determinants and Consequences.” His research examines how socio-economic, psychological, and physical health factors influence life satisfaction among diabetes patients in India.
His academic interests lie in health economics, gender studies, and public health, with a focus on understanding social and economic determinants of well-being.
Shubham teaches courses in economics, business statistics, and data analysis, integrating real-world applications with analytical and software-based learning.
title: Dr. Shubham Ranjan, Assistant Professor,

text:
Shubham teaches courses in economics, business statistics, and data analysis, integrating real-world applications with analytical and software-based learning.
He actively incorporates tools such as MS Excel, Stata, RStudio, and SPSS to strengthen students’ quantitative and decision-making abilities.
Currently, his research extends to developing a Health Insurance Equity Index (HIEI) to evaluate disparities in healthcare access, utilization, and financial protection across India.
He is passionate about evidence-based policymaking and experiential teaching, and strives to bridge research and practice to promote inclusive and sustainable development.

Biography
Dr Suprita Talnikar is an Assistant Professor of Mathematics at the Institute of Engineering & Technology, JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur.
She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata, where her doctoral research focused on theoretical cryptography.
Her research primarily concerns provable security in classical symmetric-key cryptography and authenticated encryption, with emerging interests in post-quantum symmetric-key cryptography and robust cryptography, and applied interests in secret sharing, IoT security, blockchain, privacy-preserving machine learning and AI security.

Dr. Sushant Pokhriyal
Assistant Professor
Biography
Dr.
Sushant Pokhriyal holds a Ph.D. in Mathematics from Shiv Nadar University, India, with a thesis on invariant subspaces associated with near-isometry and unicellular operators.
His research interests span Dynamical Systems, Operator Theory, Applied Harmonic Analysis, and Machine Learning, with a current focus on data-driven modeling and learning of nonlinear dynamical systems.
He studies how finite-dimensional nonlinear dynamics can be embedded into infinite-dimensional function spaces, particularly Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS), using linear operators such as the Liouville and Koopman operators.
A key component of his work is the integration of deep learning techniques to learn operator representations, latent coordinates, and reduced-order models directly from data, enabling scalable and interpretable modeling of complex dynamical processes.

Biography
Professor (Dr.) Umesh Gupta has 25 years of experience in teaching and research.
He is working as Dean of Academic Affairs and Professor in Mathematics at JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur.
His areas of expertise are Statistical Data Analysis and Optimization Techniques.
He had also worked as a Visiting Professor at St.
Cloud State University, USA.
He is a member of the American Mathematical Society, Indian Mathematical Society, Soft Computing Research Society, ISTD Jaipur, Vigyan Bharti Rajasthan, Operational Research Society of India, and the Rajasthan Academy of Physical Sciences.
Umesh Gupta is a senior member of IACSIT, Singapore.
title: Dr. Umesh Gupta, Professor And Dean Of Academic Affairs, Mathematics

text:
Umesh Gupta is a senior member of IACSIT, Singapore.
He has a number of research publications in various International & National Journals & Conference Proceedings to his credit.
Umesh Gupta has written the textbooks of Engineering Mathematics and Research Methods in Management.
Umesh Gupta was the founder and president of the Institution’s Innovation Council of MHRD, Govt. of India at JKLU, and also the core team member of the Atal Incubation Center – JKLU.
His research interest includes Statistical Data Analysis, Optimization Techniques, and Fluid Mechanics.

Biography
Dr Vijaylakshmi holds a PhD from Nirwan University, Jaipur in 2024 in the area of teaching English Language to students through English Literature.
Her other PhD is in 2013 that talks about the Trojan War and the Characterisation of Great Alexander.
In her academic career spanning around 2 decades, she has taught English literature, Accent neutralisation, English language, Life skills, and Critical thinking at Government and private universities of good repute.
Her research expertise is anchored around Greek literature and English Language Teaching (ELT).
Her research contributions have been presented in leading national as well as international conferences and published in renowned journals.

Biography
Mr.
Vishwajeet is an Assistant Professor at the Centre for Communication and Critical Thinking, JK Lakshmipat University.
His research engages evolutionary literary theory and biocultural criticism, with a focus on how literary texts represent dynamics of power, sexuality, and social competition within specific cultural and historical contexts.
He is the author of Research Methodology in Humanities and Social Sciences, a former top-seller on Amazon.in and Evolution in Pair-Bonding: A Critique of Hetero-Socio-Sexual Intercourse, a monograph detailing his MPhil research.
His recent publications with Taylor & Francis (Q1) (2026), Peter Lang (2025, 2026), Routledge (2026) Cambridge Scholars Publishing (2025), and Atlantic (2025) engage with sensory studies, diasporic disillusionment, and affect in postcolonial writing.

CODE OF CONDUCT FOR FACULTY, OFFICIALS & SUPPORT STAFF Abide by the rules, regulations and any other instructions that may be framed by the University from time to time and which are in force to regulate the work conduct and behavior of the Employee.
• Maintain all times absolute dignity integrity and devotion to duty and loyalty to JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU) and shall do nothing that would or is likely to tarnish the image or reputation of JKLU, or adversely affect its interests.
• Carry out duties and responsibilities assigned to his/her/her post and shall also carry out any other duties that may be assigned to him from time to time.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Use his/her position or influence directly or indirectly to secure employment for any person in any Institutions with which he has official dealings in connection with the business of JKLU.
• Bring or attempt to bring any outside influence to bear upon the Management to further his/her personal interests in JKLU.
• Misuse the amenities provided to him by University to discharge his/her official duties.
• Accept any gifts, presents, gratis, payments or other favours from students, suppliers, contractors, dealers or anyone who could directly or indirectly influence/damage/harm the interests/goodwill or reputation of JKLU.
• Under any circumstance divulge or make public any information imparted to or gained by him in the course of his/her duties as an Employee of JKLU or otherwise.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• All information obtained in the course of employment with JKLU shall be deemed to be strictly confidential.
All employees are precluded from revealing any such information, directly or indirectly to anyone without express written authority of the Management.
• An Employee who is in breach of the above condition shall be deemed to have breached a material condition of his/her employment with JKLU and the same will render such employee to summarily termination of his/her employment with JKLU in addition, JKLU may initiate legal action against any such employee.
• Engage directly or indirectly in any trade or business or avocation or calling or undertake any other employment, whether for consideration or not, without obtaining prior written consent of the Management.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text: • Refrain from carrying on activities that create or may potentially create a conflict between his/her personal interest and the interests of JKLU.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
The activities which create/may potentially create a conflict of interest include (but are not limited to) dealings with suppliers, customers or other entities connected howsoever with JKLU (under a contract or otherwise), including (but not limited to) the following: • According preferential treatment to entities in which substantive interest is held by the employee, his/her family members, his/her close relatives or by any entity in which substantive interest is held by of the foregoing persons and entering into any contract (written or oral) on a non-arm’s length basis by the employee, his/her family members, his/her close relatives or by entity in which substantive interest is held by any of the foregoing persons.
No Employee Shall • Propagate/indulge in communal, unionism, terrorist or sectarian activity.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
No Employee Shall • Propagate/indulge in communal, unionism, terrorist or sectarian activity.
• Discriminate against person on the grounds of caste, creed. language, gender, religion, etc.
• Indulge in or encourage any form of malpractice.
Accept private tuition.
Properties of JKLU, Every Employee Shall • Take due care of the property, materials, instruments, to safeguard; machines, furniture, cash, library documents, etc. of JKLU entrusted to his/her care and shall take all reasonable precautions to safeguard them against accident, damage, loss or pilferage.
Where damage or loss is attributable to the mishandling or misuse, such an employee shall be liable for disciplinary action as may be deemed fit by the University shall be entitled to recover the assigned/ assessed value of such breakage, damage or loss from the employee.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Promptly report any occurrence or defect noticed which might endanger lives or persons in JKLU and might result in any damage to the property of JKLU or that of any others.
• Take appropriate precautions against hazards and shall make proper use of safety devices and preventive measures as prescribed and provided by the University.
• Indemnify JKLU of any loss caused due to his/her negligence.
Unauthorized possession of goods, etc.
• An employee found in unauthorized possession of any goods, equipment’s, articles materials, etc. which are in use in JKLU or kept in stock in JKLU and are not normally carried by the person, will be deemed to have got into possession of such goods by improper means.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
The University may confiscate such goods and such unauthorized possession attracts disciplinary action as well as any other action as deemed fit by the University.
Unauthorized persons in the premises An employee who has been suspended, laid off, discharged, dismissed or has resigned or is not working for any reason, shall leave University premises forthwith unless required to stay back by the Management.
Such employees shall not enter JKLU premises without permission.
Possession/Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Narcotics Employee shall not be under the influence of intoxicating drinks/drugs while on duty.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
Possession/Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Narcotics Employee shall not be under the influence of intoxicating drinks/drugs while on duty.
Other Terms & Conditions • Employee will devote whole time to the service of the University and will not, without having first obtained permission of the competent authority, apply or accept any assignment/post or service with/without remuneration or apply and proceed for higher studies.
• During the tenure of engagement with the University, employee will conform to all the rules and regulations of the University governing the services of its employees as applicable from time to time.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Neither during the engagement with University nor afterwards, employee will give anyone by word of mouth or otherwise any particulars or details of our financial matters, technical know-how, client information, IT software of JKLU, data security arrangements, administrative and/or organizational matters whether confidential, secret or otherwise which employee acquire during the course of employment.
Employee will also not use at any time such information, which is of confidential nature for employee personal gains.
• Employee will not seek election to any legislature or local body without permission of the competent authority in writing.
• After joining University, employee will communicate to the appointing authority the changes in their present/permanent address, educational/professional qualifications or of any other particulars given by employee in the application form.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• No employee shall, except with the prior permission of JKLU or in the bonafide discharge of his/her duties, participate in a Radio/TV broadcast, give speech to
public, or contribute any article or write any letter to any newspaper or periodical or publish any pamphlet anonymously or pseudonymously or in his/her own name, on a subject which may have a bearing on the affairs of JKLU or detrimental to the image/interests of JKLU.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
Criticism of Management No employee shall criticize the University either in the press or over the radio or on any public platform, social media, provided, however, that nothing in this rule shall apply to any statement made or views expressed by an employee in his/her official capacity or in the due performance of the duties assigned to him.
Unauthorized Communication of Information No employee shall, except in accordance with any general or special order of JKLU, or in the bonafide performance of the duties assigned to him, communicate directly or indirectly any official document or information to any employee or any other person.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
Unauthorized Publication of Official Documents No employee, while in service of the University or after retirement, resignation, dismissal or discharge, shall make public or publish any documents, papers or information which might have come into his/her possession in his/her official capacity, without obtaining prior written permission from the University.
Misconduct Interpretation “Misconduct” shall mean an act of omission or commission, express or implied, custom or urge, whether specified herein or otherwise, either singly or in collaboration with others, whether amounting to a substantive act, abetment or connivance committed within the premises of JKLU, if related to the maintenance of discipline or pertaining to the interest of the University or other employees or officers of the University.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
Any act of omission/ commission/indiscipline which affects the reputation or prestige of the University or any act or conduct unbecoming of an employee of JKLU or any breach of these service rules shall amount to misconduct whether committed within or outside the premises of JKLU.
Acts of Misconduct • Misconduct on the part of an employee shall entail disciplinary action as specified herein.
• Followings an illustrative but not exhaustive list of acts of omission and commission and any other action which may be construed as indiscipline or Misconduct.
• Willful insubordination or disobedience of any lawful and reasonable order of the superior.
• Commission of any acts subversive of discipline or good behavior.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Willful insubordination or disobedience of any lawful and reasonable order of the superior.
• Commission of any acts subversive of discipline or good behavior.
• Participation in any strike/demonstration, or any other kind of agitation or abetting and inciting such agitation or abetting and inciting such agitation activities in contravention of any law.
• Theft, fraud, dishonesty, embezzlement, misappropriation in connection with work/ property of JKLU.
• Willful damage to property or loss or damage to property owing to negligence or subversive or unethical practices.
• Demanding or accepting or giving bribes or any illegal gratification whatsoever.
Absence without leave for more than seven consecutive days.
• Habitual late attendance or habitually leaving work before time or absence from place of work.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
Absence without leave for more than seven consecutive days.
• Habitual late attendance or habitually leaving work before time or absence from place of work.
Loitering while on duty and after duty in JKLU premises.
• Negligence or neglect of work.
• Accepting service for any consideration inside or outside the institutional/unit premises without the approval of the University.
• Drunkenness, fighting, riotous, disorderly or indecent behavior in JKLU premises and public places, affecting the reputation of JKLU.
• Giving false evidence or statement in any domestic enquiry held by JKLU or in a case conducted in a Court of Law in which JKLU is a party.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Travelling or carrying unauthorized passengers, materials in any of JKLU’s vehicles without valid authority, or otherwise using JKLU’s vehicle for personal use without prior approval from the University.
• Collection or canvassing for collection of any money for any purpose within JKLU premises without prior permission.
• Smoking in the office or in any other place where smoking is specifically prohibited.
• Sleeping while on duty.
• Distribution or exhibiting inside JKLU premises hand-bills, pamphlets or posters without written prior permission of the Management.
• Attending or holding any unauthorized meeting within JKLU premises.
• Unauthorized disclosure or information about the business or affairs of JKLU.
• Gambling or canvassing for sale of any commodities, chit funds.
Lottery tickets or coupons etc. within JKLU premises.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Gambling or canvassing for sale of any commodities, chit funds.
Lottery tickets or coupons etc. within JKLU premises.

Procedure for Enquiries & Punishment The University shall be authorized to delegate the powers to any member of the University for the purpose of administering these service rules or for ordering and enquiry and awarding punishment.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• Any employee found to commit any act of misconducts shall be served with a charge sheet clearly stating the charges levelled against him.
Such and employee shall be given an opportunity to explain and answer the charges levelled against him in an enquiry conducted by an enquiry officer duly appointed by the Management for this purpose.
• The employee concerned shall be given an opportunity to lead evidence to the charges and produce documents and witnesses in support his/her defence and cross examine the witnesses on whose evidence the charges are based.
The employee concerned, if he so desires he shall be allowed to be defended by a co-employee of JKLU, on the condition that such other employee may not be paid any consideration for such defence.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
The statements of the Management and the Employee and the evidence lead by either side shall be recorded by the Enquiry Officer.
If the Employee concerned fails to attend the enquiry, it shall be proceeded ex-parte.
The enquiry officer shall submit his/her findings to the Management based on the evidence recorded and documents produced during the enquiry.
• An employee against whom misconduct is alleged may be suspended from duty without pay or allowance, pending enquiry.
The order of suspension shall take effect immediately on its communication to the employee.
An employee under suspension pending enquiry shall be eligible to subsistence allowance.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
An employee under suspension pending enquiry shall be eligible to subsistence allowance.
However, the subsistence allowance shall not be payable for the period of any adjournment of postponement of the enquiry expressly sought for by the employee and granted by the enquiry officer.
• If an employee is held guilty of misconduct as a result of the enquiry punishments awarded to him, the employee shall not be entitled to any salary /wages during the period of his/her suspension.
• Result of the enquiry, an employee is found not guilty misconduct, he shall be entitled to receive the difference of the subsistence allowance paid if any and the emoluments he would have received had he not been-suspended for the period of this suspension pending enquiry.
title: Code Of Conduct Employees

text:
• An employee found guilty of misconduct after domestic enquiry may be punished by imposition of one or more minor or major penalties.

A copy of such order passed by the Management shall be served on the Employee concerned.
• In case of dismissal, the employee may appeal within 30 days of receipt of such order to the Appellate Authority whose decision will be final.

title: Code Of Conduct Students

text: Under the provisions of the said Regulation, ragging has inter-alia been defined as any conduct by any student / students whether by words spoken or written or an act which has an effect of teasing treating or handling with rudeness a fresher or any other student or indulging in rowdy or indisciplinary activities which causes or is likely to cause annoyance, hardship or psychological harm or creates fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any other student or forcing a student to do an act which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame or torment or embarrassment so as to affect the physique or psyche of a fresher or any other student, showing of power, authority or superiority by a student to any fresher or any other student.

text:

These punishments include suspension from attending classes, withholding / withdrawing scholarship, debarring from appearing in the test / examination, withholding results, suspension / debarring from hostel, cancellation of admission, rustication from the institution for certain period and expulsion from the institution.
title: Code Of Conduct Students

text:

Course Objective: This course is designed to enhance the academic writing skills of Ph.D. students, focusing on key writing strategies necessary for successful academic communication. The course will provide in-depth coverage of writing structures, academic conventions, argumentation, clarity, and revision strategies, allowing students to effectively communicate their research in dissertations, articles, and presentations. Through targeted exercises and feedback, students will develop the skills necessary for high- quality academic writing in their respective fields. |  |  |  |  |  |
title: PhD Coursework Handbook 2024-25

text: Learning Outcomes: On successful completion of this course, participants should be able to: 1) Write clearly and concisely, demonstrating a coherent and logical structure in their academic writing. 2) Develop and present arguments effectively while synthesizing existing literature and research. 3) Employ strategies for revising drafts to improve coherence, style, and academic tone. 4) Use appropriate citation styles and adhere to ethical standards in academic writing, including avoiding plagiarism. 5) Engage with peer feedback constructively and refine their work based on critical reviews. 6) Write key sections of their dissertations or research papers with attention to scholarly conventions. |  |  |  |  |  |
title: PhD Coursework Handbook 2024-25

text:
Assessment Scheme: 1. Writing Assignments (60%) o Students will submit ten short writing assignments during the course. These assignments will be assessed based on clarity, structure, argumentation, and adherence to academic conventions. 2. Final Project (30%) o The final assignment is a piece of writing criticizing journal article(s) that incorporates the skills learned during the course. Students will be assessed on structure, argumentation, clarity, and appropriate use of academic conventions. 3. Class Participation (10%) o Active participation in class discussions, feedback sessions, and activities will be monitored throughout the course. |  |  |  |  |  |

Course code: Course Syllabus
Session 1: Introduction to Academic Writing (2 hours)
• Overview of the course and expectations
• Introduction to the writing process: planning, drafting, and revising
• Understanding the purpose and structure of academic writing
• Writing for scholarly audiences: tone, style, and purpose
Session 2: Crafting Clear and Effective Academic Prose (2 hours)
• Sentence-level clarity: avoiding wordiness and jargon
• Maintaining a formal and objective tone
title: PhD Coursework Handbook 2024-25

text:
Session 2: Crafting Clear and Effective Academic Prose (2 hours)
• Sentence-level clarity: avoiding wordiness and jargon
• Maintaining a formal and objective tone
• Active vs. passive voice and its usage in academic writing
• Developing precise and concise writing
Session 3: Structuring an Argument (3 hours)
• Building a clear research question or thesis statement
• Developing logical and coherent arguments
• Structuring paragraphs for flow and coherence
• Organizing research findings and evidence effectively
Session 4: Writing the Literature Review (2 hours)
• Purpose and function of the literature review
• Synthesizing sources and highlighting gaps in research
• Organizing the literature review (thematic, chronological, methodological)
• Writing critical, rather than descriptive, reviews
Session 5: Writing the Introduction and Conclusion (2 hours)
title: PhD Coursework Handbook 2024-25

text:
• Organizing the literature review (thematic, chronological, methodological)
• Writing critical, rather than descriptive, reviews
Session 5: Writing the Introduction and Conclusion (2 hours)
• Crafting an engaging introduction that outlines research aims and questions
• Writing clear and concise conclusions that summarize findings and suggest further research
• Connecting the introduction and conclusion to the overall research narrative
Session 6: Research Methodology and Data Presentation (2 hours)
• Writing about research design and methodology
• Presenting data clearly and logically
• Explaining qualitative and quantitative research methods effectively
• Writing results and interpretation in academic style
Session 7: Revising and Editing for Clarity and Style (3 hours)
• Self-revision techniques: improving clarity, coherence, and flow
• Peer review practice: how to give and receive constructive feedback

• Peer review practice: how to give and receive constructive feedback

• Overview of citation styles (APA, MLA, Chicago, etc.)
• How to properly cite and reference sources
• Understanding plagiarism and how to avoid it
• Ethical considerations in academic writing
Session 9: Writing for Publication (2 hours)
• Tailoring writing for academic journals and conferences
• Writing abstracts, cover letters, and preparing manuscripts for submission
• Responding to reviewer feedback and revising for publication
• Common pitfalls in academic writing and how to overcome them

Course Description:
Consumer behavior is one of the most interesting and important aspects of marketing management.
Virtually all decisions involved in developing an effective marketing mix for a product or service rely on thorough knowledge of the consumers who comprise the target market.

This course explores the interdisciplinary dimensions of supply chain management and strategic
importance of good supply chain design, planning and operations in the economic development of

affect the economy. Within the strategic framework of SCM the course identifies facilities,
inventory, transportation, information, sourcing and pricing as the key drivers of supply chain
performance.

performance
